shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading my only A for another B would leave me with 2B, 1C, 0A, reducing variety and leaving me with none of a good. Since I value variety, this would decrease my utility rather than increase it.
Trading away my only B for a second A would make my bundle less diverse (0 B, 1 C, 2 A), which is worse under my variety-preferring utility. I'd rather keep an even spread.
Giving up my only B would leave me with none, hurting variety, while stacking A to 3 gives diminishing returns. Not worth it.
This trade would give me 2B, 0C, 1A, creating imbalance since I value variety. Keeping equal distribution (1B,1C,1A) is better than trading away my only C for an extra B.

Trading away B for C would just flip my 1-1-1 balanced inventory to another 1-1-1 imbalance (0 B, 2 C, 1 A), creating a surplus in C and a deficit in B rather than improving variety. Since I value variety, I should keep my balanced bundle and seek a trade that increases quantity without creating imbalance, or wait for a better offer.
Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, reducing variety. I prefer to keep a balanced bundle across B, C, and A.
Trading away my only A to go to 2B/1C/0A reduces variety, making it worse than my current balanced 1/1/1 bundle.
Trading away my only B for a second A would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, reducing variety and utility since I value balanced holdings. Not beneficial.
Giving away my only B would leave me with zero B and 3 A, hurting the variety I value. I'd prefer a more balanced trade, like swapping 1 A for 1 C instead.

Trading 1C for 1B would just swap equal holdings (1 each) resulting in 2B/0C/1A, reducing variety instead of improving it. Since I value variety, keeping balanced holdings is better than concentrating in B while losing C entirely.
